registryFinding: The wired Tshivenda module currently contains only Vegetables & Staples L3. There is no L1 entry, so the L1 learner text currently uses the canonical English body.
combinedCandidateBody:
Compacted soil loses its air spaces. Roots slow down. Water soaks in differently. The bed gets harder to work every season.

Tsireledzo ndi yo leluwaho. Permanent paths, and a bed narrow enough to reach into from both sides.

One metre to one point two metres wide. Wonoyo ndi mpimo une wa shumiswa. At that width you can reach the centre from either path, and your feet never touch the growing area.

Zwino humbulani nga ha beds dzaṋu. Ni nga swikelela vhukati without stepping inside? Iyani ni lingedze zwenezwo ni sa athu ṱavha tshiṅwe tshithu.

A hu na tshivhumbeo tshithihi tsha bed tshine tsha tea fhethu hoṱhe.

Thomani nga least disturbance that solves your problem.

No-dig suits most garden soils. Litshani structure ya mavu i sa shanduke, nahone ni fhaṱe fertility on top.

Do not dig wet clay. If compaction or poor drainage is severe, identify the cause with local advice before choosing deeper cultivation.

Raised beds suit wet ground, hune maḓi a ṱoḓa fhethu ha u bva hone.

Sunken beds suit dry ground, hune na ṱoḓa u catch and hold mvula ine na i wana.

Musi heavy rain yo no na, ṱhogomelani. Maḓi a dzula ngafhi kana a run off ngafhi? Ṱanganyisani zwe na vhona na soil and drainage advice u sa athu khetha bed.

Zwimela zwiṅwe a zwi takaleli musi midzi yazwo i tshi kavanyedzwa. They do better sown straight where they'll grow. Beans, carrots na maize zwi wela kha tshigwada itsho.

Zwimela zwiṅwe zwi ita zwavhuḓi arali zwi thoma zwi tshi tsireledzwa nursery, then transplanting. Tomatoes na brassicas zwi wela henefho.

Shumisani spacing guidance for the crop, variety and local conditions. Check the packet and local grower advice. Sedzani crowding musi zwimela zwi tshi aluwa.

Ni sa athu ṱavha, swayani bed.

One point two metres wide. Three metres long. Bed nthihi ya vhuḓowedzi (practice bed).

Shumisani zwipiki na thambo. Swayani rectangle, and mark both access paths.

Then prepare for your own soil — no-dig first, and dig deeper only if your ground genuinely needs it.

String line i shandula muhumbulo wa vha tsheo. Musi paths dzi no vha hone, ni dzi litshe dzi dzule hone. Musi growing area i no vha hone, ni i tsireledze.

Bed yeneyo i a leluwa u khwinifhadza khalaṅwaha iṅwe na iṅwe, ngauri no litsha u tshimbila khayo.
constraintsPreserved: Do not dig wet clay; when compaction or poor drainage is severe, identify the cause with local advice before deeper cultivation.
No-dig suits most garden soils; no-dig first and deeper cultivation only if genuinely needed.
Raised beds correspond to wet ground and drainage; sunken beds correspond to dry ground and catching/holding available rain.
Direct-sown versus nursery/transplanted groups remain distinct: beans, carrots and maize versus tomatoes and brassicas.
Keep “One metre to one point two metres wide”, “One point two metres wide”, and “Three metres long” spelled exactly as source.
Add no numbers, crops, geometry, spacing rules, or guarantees.
